l1_connect_account.title: Enrol sites and tenants that are outside the platform
l1_connect_account.why: The site exists in your asset records, in the identity provider or in procurement, but no agent reports to the platform, so nothing there is prevented, detected or inventoried.
steps: Find the owner of the site (IT operations or the business unit) and what stopped the rollout: change windows, an incumbent product, missing rights.
Agree a pilot ring of 5% of devices and a date for full rollout.
Automate enrolment (device management, group policy or a golden image) so new devices arrive protected.
l1_connect_account.success: Every known site reports to the platform and new devices enrol on their own.

l1_auto_onboarding.title: Enrol new sites automatically
l1_auto_onboarding.why: New sites keep appearing and each waits for a manual rollout, so the gap reopens every quarter.
steps: Put the agent in the device build (golden image, MDM profile, endpoint configuration management).
Alert the TAM when a site appears in procurement or the directory and has no agent within 14 days.
l1_auto_onboarding.success: New sites are enrolled within 14 days without anyone raising a ticket.

l2_enable_inventory.title: Get coverage on the device types the platform does not see
l2_enable_inventory.why: Some device classes at connected sites report no agents, so the platform cannot say what is running there.
steps: List the device classes with no agents (servers, VDI, mobile, Linux nodes) and the blocker for each.
Start with servers and domain controllers: they carry the most risk per device.
Confirm coverage against the asset records, not against the platform's own list.
l2_enable_inventory.success: Every expected device class at a connected site has agents reporting.
